newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda says it wants aid, not force.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda says it wants aid, not force.

text.p: Rwandan Vice-President Paul Kagame said on Wednesday he was suspicious of the need to link humanitarian aid for thousands of returning refugees to the presence of an international force in Rwanda.
"If humanitarian assistance is tied to a force, then I am right to be suspicious," he told a news conference.

Kagame, who is considered the most powerful man in the Tutsi-dominated government, said the return last week of over half a million Hutu refugees from eastern Zaire created the need for aid, not arms.

The countries that have agreed to participate in the intervention force, originally intended to help feed refugees in eastern Zaire and help them return home, have called a meeting in Germany, now set for Friday.
Zairean rebels fighting government troops and Rwandan Hutu forces in eastern Zaire sparked the mass exodus of refugees that began last Friday.
Kagame said he believed the number of refugees remaining in eastern Zaire -- which aid agencies and western governments say could be 500,000 or more -- had been exaggerated.
"The numbers have been inflated," he said. "I believe the majority of refugees have returned...The situation has drastically and dramatically changed."
